newsitem.title: USA: Newsletter says Greenspan persuades Rivlin, Meyer.
newsitem.headline: Newsletter says Greenspan persuades Rivlin, Meyer.

text.p: A newsletter said Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan had overcome the opposition of his deputy Alice Rivlin and Fed Governor Laurence Meyer for another interest rate increase.

Without naming any sources, the Evans-Novak Political Report's April 29 edition said Greespan "appears to have locked in one more interest rate increase, sheduled for the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting."

"Greenspan has apparently secured their support by 1) making clear how very much he wants this second increase, and 2) assuring them that there will not be a third hike at the July 1 meeting," the newsletter said.
The Evans and Novak report also said Meyer and Rivlin privately disagreed with the increase enacted at the March 25 meeting.

Meyer, in the text of an April 24 speech reported by Reuters, said he supported the March 25 quarter point rise in the federal funds rate because of concern about "persistent strength in aggregate demand."
A Fed spokesman declined to comment on the newsletter report.
